chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, all from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Abdul Samad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a believing servant commits a sin, Allah grants him a respite of seven hours. If he seeks forgiveness from Allah, no record is kept against him; but if the hours pass and he does not seek forgiveness, one evil deed is recorded against him. Indeed, the believer is reminded of his sin even after twenty years, so he seeks forgiveness from his Lord and He forgives him; whereas the unbeliever forgets it from the moment he commits it.
ai.seo_question: How long does Allah give a believer to repent before a sin is recorded?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'tadhiir' (delayed recording) in Shia theology, illustrating the balance between divine justice and mercy by granting believers a grace period to repent. It contrasts the believer's persistent self-awareness of sin, which motivates continuous repentance even after decades, with the disbeliever's spiritual heedlessness. This mechanism underscores the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of immediate tawbah and the enduring nature of God's forgiveness for those who remain conscious of their faults.
